Block-cut locality reduces the graph to independent bridge or triangle edge-terminal electrical circuits. Three closed-form triangle resistances and the arithmetic-geometric-mean inequality strictly force equal priced spokes at any global minimizer. Differentiating the exact two-piece scalar objective produces all three k(t) branches, transition prices 2/5 and 4, and the complete equality set at t=4. Summing required block budgets gives the global lower bound K/B with equality by constructive allocation. A 562-assertion rational verifier including full grounded Laplacian independently checks representative cases; finite checks are not cited as a universal proof.

value.rationale: Provides a closed-form budget law and every globally optimal edge conductance for a natural infinite family of fault-tolerant consensus networks, not just one finite graph. The two nontrivial exact thresholds expose a counterintuitive equal-conductance plateau despite unequal edge prices and a sharp backup-edge deletion transition. General cactus assembly composes local k(t) coefficients regardless of block arrangement, and price-four provides an exact continuum of otherwise isolated unique optimizers. The mathematical design target is a legitimate adversarial stability margin; it is not merely a normalization or negative-edge sign check.
